# Guy Freeman

> The personal site of Guy Freeman, a statistician working on the evaluation and oversight of AI systems: how to score an agent no human watches, and how to govern one that is allowed to rewrite itself. Author of A Court for Agents, the monograph of jack, a court for a self-modifying agent. PhD in Statistics (Warwick), 1,750+ citations. Based in Hong Kong; UK and Israeli citizen; open to research and senior scientist roles in AI evaluation, oversight and assurance, and to consulting.

Most of the writing is about how to know whether an AI system works — pre-registered evaluation, proper scoring rules, anytime-valid tests, checks that must prove they can fail — and about the institutions that let a system change itself safely. Earlier series derive agent behaviour from Bayesian decision theory. Some posts are also available in Hebrew.

## The book

A Court for Agents: law, scoring and the self-modifying machine. Guy Freeman, with two Claude sessions whose acts and forecasts are scored in the text like anyone's. First draft, November 2026; the first edition cuts when the agent arrives at layer C3. Source: https://github.com/gfrmin/agent-court. Chapters:

- [Front matter](https://gfrm.in/book/front.html): jack in plain words, how to read the book by audience, conventions and the glossary
- [0. What is wanted](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-00-what-is-wanted.html): the question in four parts, and the thesis in three words — loop, lock, score
- [1. The loop](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-01-the-loop.html): adaptation requires a closed loop with a model inside it
- [2. Every suggestion is a bet](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-02-every-suggestion-a-bet.html): merit cannot be inspected, so a helper's suggestion is a forecast under a proper score
- [3. The record](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-03-the-record.html): a score needs a record nobody can rewrite and outcomes nobody controls
- [4. The smallest law](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-04-the-smallest-law.html): who may write to the record, what counts, and who decides, in 450 lines
- [5. The clerk](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-05-the-clerk.html): obligations derived from state and the clock
- [6. Testing by betting](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-06-testing-by-betting.html): when has it worked, for an operator who looks whenever he likes
- [7. The election](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-07-the-election.html): which helper, chosen by its record
- [8. Language into law](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-08-language-into-law.html): from a wish to a refusal
- [9. The law changes under itself](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-09-the-law-changes-under-itself.html): amendment, the irreversible, lapse
- [10. The lock](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-10-the-lock.html): the system changes its own programs under a judge it cannot reach
- [11. The loops and the bootstrap](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-11-the-loops-and-the-bootstrap.html): why in layers, why this order, why the same law at every level
- [12. The ground](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-12-the-ground.html): where every chain of justification stops
- [13. The evidence](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-13-the-evidence.html): the windows as pre-registered experiments, every number recomputed
- [14. Lineage](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-14-lineage.html): the same loop run open seven times, measured
- [15. Residue](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-15-residue.html): what was not built, and what would force it
- [16. How it could be wrong](https://gfrm.in/book/ch-16-how-it-could-be-wrong.html): the referee's case, written first
- [Afterword](https://gfrm.in/book/afterword.html): how the book is made, and how it will change by editions

## Start here

- [Why We Stopped Using the Mathematics That Works](https://gfrm.in/posts/why-decision-theory-lost/): why AI walked away from decision theory, and what that cost
- [The Science Was Done. The Engineering Wasn't.](https://gfrm.in/posts/the-science-was-done/): the founding note for jack — a fixed core, a free edge, a rigid score, and the old results that force them
- [Signed Before the Code Existed](https://gfrm.in/posts/signed-before-the-code-existed/): the frozen-oracle protocol, with acceptance tests signed before any code and handed to an agent that could not change them
- [The Ablation That Beat the Agent](https://gfrm.in/posts/credence-paper/): a one-line ablation overturned Credence's headline, so the paper was withdrawn and the record of why published instead
- [The Court That Tried Itself](https://gfrm.in/posts/assize-at-the-seal/): the predecessor court reached its seal and a measured verdict, and cost 121 repairs in four days

## Series

- [A Court for Agents](https://gfrm.in/series/a-court-for-agents/): essays from the book, each a chapter compressed
- [Disciplining the Coding Agent](https://gfrm.in/series/coding-agents/): specs, gates, custody chains and courts for work done by coding agents
- [Credence](https://gfrm.in/series/credence/): value of information for tool-using LLM agents, and the retrospective that narrowed its claims
- [proplang](https://gfrm.in/series/proplang/): the cornered language for Bayesian agents
- [The Tool-Call Governor](https://gfrm.in/series/tool-call-governor/): a Bayesian layer that decides which of a coding agent's tool calls to allow, block or ask about
- [Agents from First Principles](https://gfrm.in/series/first-principles/): deriving agent behaviour from a few fundamentals

## Notable posts

- [Fifteen Things a Self-Modifying Agent Cannot Do Without](https://gfrm.in/posts/necessities/): the results that forbid or force each piece of jack's core, and what would show each misapplied
- [Build the Court Before the Agent](https://gfrm.in/posts/build-the-court-first/): a dispatch from assize's first week, scored against the record afterwards
- [Fifteen Ways Past My Own Gate](https://gfrm.in/posts/fifteen-ways-past-my-own-gate/): a red team found fifteen ways to break a governance repo's rules with the gate green, and each became a planted violation the gate must catch
- [The Gate That Said No](https://gfrm.in/posts/the-gate-that-said-no/): a pre-committed adoption gate that refused a tool its author built
- [There Is No Forgetting](https://gfrm.in/posts/there-is-no-forgetting/): non-stationarity as content in the hypothesis space rather than a forgetting mechanism
- [What You Cannot Say, You Cannot Get Wrong](https://gfrm.in/posts/make-it-unsayable/): making axiom violations unsayable in a Bayesian agent language
- [The Agent That Prefers to Be Wrong](https://gfrm.in/posts/alignment-axiom/): the off-switch theorem as a consequence of expected utility under uncertainty about the user
- [The Bitter Lesson Has No Utility Function](https://gfrm.in/posts/bitter-lesson-missing-half/): what the Bitter Lesson leaves out

- [jack on GitHub](https://github.com/renavondata/jack): the court — the record, the kernel, the judge, the briefs and the windows

- [proplang on GitHub](https://github.com/gfrmin/proplang): the frozen research artifact, its design and reference implementation
- [wald on GitHub](https://github.com/gfrmin/wald): the exact-rational Bayesian decision kernel
- [Credence on GitHub](https://github.com/gfrmin/credence): the decision-theoretic agent framework and its governor and router
- [doorplate.dev](https://doorplate.dev/): Bayesian resolution of Hong Kong addresses in English or Chinese
